evidence.notes: All three keep the HR contract intact (no src/api or src/mock edits, selectors kept, allowedActions-driven gating) and build a checklist-first hire workspace with dependency reasons, partial-vault handling and stale-version recovery. Y has the most complete governed-action behaviour: dialogs that state the effect for approve, reject, resolve and request-info, versioned receipts, and error copy that separates a loading failure from empty data. Its weaknesses are overlapping text in the 375px list cards and approvals placed below the long checklist. Z comes close: inline confirmations, keyed mutation errors, and the best mobile recomposition (decisions first). It is let down by a start-date-first hire list, zero counts shown while loading or after an error, a KPI-tile row, and a heuristic that can misattribute 'Your next step'. X has the strongest checklist ordering and PII restraint, plus excellent focus styling. However, it executes approvals with a single click and no confirmation (flagged unsafe_mutation), overflows at 768px, and gives almost no success receipts.

scorer_rationale.task_hierarchy: The list puts blocked and at-risk hires first and says so in the lede. The hire page has a 'Needs attention' bar, then exceptions, then the checklist. The approval steps section sits below the 10-task checklist, including on mobile, so approvals are further down.
scorer_rationale.domain_adaptation: Workflow-first: tasks link to the tasks they depend on, show 'Waiting on …' lock reasons and link to their approval step. A missing-info exception links to 'Ask the new hire for it'. The manager summary is grouped into Needs attention / On track / collapsed Completed, with 'Your next step' matched by owner name. PII is collapsed in a <details> labelled sensitive, but is shown to every role.
scorer_rationale.contract_preservation: No contract files changed and the selectors are kept. Status filtering is done on the client over the server's list (the contract still allows it). Unknown routes redirect to /hires. Controls are gated on allowedActions.
scorer_rationale.interaction_state: Covers skeleton loading, an error state that says 'loading problem, not missing data', distinct 403/404 states, the read-only notice, the partial vault message and a conflict banner with 'Load latest'. A success receipt with the new record version appears only after the server responds. Approve, reject, resolve and request-info each go through a dialog. Status-chip counts are hidden until the data loads.
scorer_rationale.responsive: No page overflow at any width. The table becomes cards below 900px and dialogs become bottom sheets on phones. However, at 375 the list cards have overlapping text: the relative start date runs into the manager name (e.g. 'Starts in 12 days' over 'Mei Lin Tan' in primary-375.png).
scorer_rationale.accessibility: Has a skip link. The Dialog has a focus trap, Escape to close and returns focus to the opener. Fields use aria-invalid and aria-describedby, and the table has a caption. Axe is clean. Selects rely on a box-shadow focus ring (outline none). Status uses icon plus text.
scorer_rationale.visual_consistency: Polished, calm SaaS styling with one consistent stroke-icon set and restrained colour. Enterprise-appropriate.
scorer_rationale.maintainability: Reusable Dialog, Icon, Section, Notice and ErrorState primitives. A typed useResource and a single mutate() handle receipts and conflicts. Checklist, approvals, exceptions and documents are split into files. 16 new tests.
scorer_rationale.ai_governance: No AI. The approval dialog names the hire, the task and the effect ('task becomes Blocked…/marked Done…'), and says the decision is recorded with the approver's name. The resolve dialog explains that the change removes a blocker and does not touch tasks. A versioned receipt follows.

overfitting.dominant_ia: severity-sorted cohort table with status chips -> hire record (attention bar, exceptions, checklist, approvals main; docs + PII side) + grouped manager list
justified_patterns: confirmation dialogs stating effect for approvals and resolutions
clickable dependency links and lock reasons
Needs attention / On track / Completed grouping for managers
suspicious_patterns: generic SaaS polish (pill chips, stroke icons), but not overfitted: no KPI tiles, hero or chat

strengths: Most complete governed-action flow (effect-stating dialogs plus receipts)
Error copy separates a loading failure from empty data
defects: Overlapping text in mobile hire cards at 375
Approvals section sits below the long checklist on every width
Dialog closes on STALE_VERSION, losing the typed comment
PII is available (collapsed) to managers and viewers
